_README: IntentOps reference saddle -- hook wiring for this host runtime.
Copy the 'hooks' block below into the project's settings file, or copy this
whole file to .claude/settings.json in a project that has none. See the
package README for what each hook is and what breaks without it.
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments. This host ignores unknown
keys; they are here because JSON has no comment syntax and a wiring file
nobody can read is a wiring file nobody checks.
The entries map onto four of the five saddle operations, plus one audit:
PreToolUse   -> S1 classify, S2 decide, S5 halt   (the only refusal site)
SessionStart -> imprint integrity re-hash, THEN S4 boot corpus
S2 is the one that cannot be satisfied by this file alone: it is a promise
the HOST makes, that a refusal from the pre-tool hook actually stops the
call. Removing the PreToolUse entry does not degrade the gate, it deletes it.
_SESSION_START_ORDER: The integrity re-hash runs FIRST, before the boot corpus, and the order is
the point. The corpus hook prints the node's rules into the window; the
integrity hook answers whether those rules are still the ones the imprint
manifest claims. Printed first, the answer is in front of the window before
it reads a single refusal -- and a window told that its own rules drifted
can act on that, where a window told afterwards has already read them.
It exits non-zero on drift. This host has no refusal channel at session
start (see the package README), so a named, loud banner naming the drifted
files is the strongest honest act available. It is an AUDIT, not a gate:
nothing here stops the session, and pretending otherwise would be the kind
of claim this project exists to refuse.
_INSTALL: 4. run the node's own birth check before trusting any of it
Step 3 matters more than it looks. A hook that is wired but broken is
indistinguishable from a hook that is wired and permissive, because both
of them let everything through quietly.
